Subject: Post-renewal stress validation + SLA checklist for Dedicated pool expansion

Hi Sara —

Congrats again on the renewal. Per our conversation, this thread is to coordinate the post-renewal expansion verification run for your new Dedicated pool (additional 8x A100s, pinned pool for region-us-west). Goal is to validate throughput and the new latency SLOs before we transition the production traffic routing.

Summary of what we plan to run the week of Aug 3:
- Two controlled stress windows (pre-scheduled): Aug 4 09:00-12:00 PDT and Aug 4 15:00-18:00 PDT
- Workload: mix of prompt lengths (avg 64 tokens), 80/20 chat:batch ratio, peak concurrency target 420 rps sustained for 20 minutes
- Acceptance criteria: 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for short prompts, token generation cost within the committed rate, zero failed streams > 0.1%
- Observability: Grafana dashboard + trace sampling (links at the end)

Requested from you before we land tests:
1) Confirm the target sustained concurrency you want us to validate (420 rps was discussed — confirm or update).
2) Confirm the list of IP ranges that should be allowed for the test clients (we’ll provide test agents from our dedicated pool).
3) Point of contact on your side for emergency rollback (name + phone) during the windows.

Deliverables we will provide after tests: load test report (PDF), runbook changes (PR), and a short handoff call where ops signs the acceptance checklist.

Attachments: none on this email — we’ll push the load test artifacts after the run.

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on the three items above and we’ll lock the windows.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 18:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-renewal stress validation + SLA checklist for Dedicated pool expansion

Team / Sara —

Load test completed across both windows. Quick summary (full report attached):

- Configuration: Dedicated pool expanded to +8x A100 (v5 equivalent). Autoscaling disabled for test; capacity pinned to the reserved pool.
- Workload: average prompt 64 tokens, 80% chat, 20% batch. Traffic replayed from production traces with synthetics for edge cases.
- Peak sustained: 420 rps for 20 minutes (passed). Burst: 600 rps for 10 minutes — redwood served bursts with graceful degradation.

Results (detailed percentiles in attached PDF):
- 50th percentile latency (response start): 48ms
- 95th percentile latency: 112ms (meets acceptance <=120ms)
- Error rate: 0.07% (below the 0.1% threshold)
- Stream failures: 3 total transient resets during the 600 rps spike; all recovered automatically via request retry policy. Root cause: a kernel eviction on one node during GPU memory pressure — mitigated by increasing KV cache allocation in the runtime for this pool.

Action items completed as part of the run:
- Increased KV cache allocation to reduce kernel eviction risk (patch rolled to pool).
- Updated per-route batching thresholds to prioritize short prompts during bursts.
- Instrumented additional traces for tokenization hotspots.

Attachments: acme_loadtest_report-20260804.pdf (20 pages, includes raw traces, resource utilization charts, and the acceptance checklist pre-populated).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Run a short post-patch sanity run tomorrow morning (10 minutes at 450 rps) to validate the KV cache change behaved under sustained load.
2) Jordan to share the populated acceptance checklist with procurement for signature.
3) Enable 1% trace sampling for 48 hours and schedule a 30-minute handoff call to review the report.

If Sara/procurement are happy with the attached report, we can consider this milestone accepted and mark the expansion as complete from Redwood's side.

—
Diego Fernandez
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Attachment: acme_loadtest_report-20260804.pdf
